walkthroughs.body_html:
Themes in the Synoptic Gospels — a core area of A-Level Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Themes in the Synoptic Gospels brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Themes in the Synoptic Gospels.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: How do samsara, karma and moksha fit together in Hindu thought?
options: Samsara, karma and moksha are three separate Hindu deities.
Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Samsara is the cycle of rebirth; karma is the law of action and consequence that drives rebirth; moksha is liberation from samsara — these form a connected chain, not three independent ideas.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.

mcqs.q: What is substance dualism about mind and body?
options: Substance dualism means men and women are different.
Substance dualism is the belief that humans have two personalities.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.
The view (associated with Descartes) that mind and body are two distinct kinds of substance — a non-physical mind interacting with a physical body.
